subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Alex — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent latency when serving long-form summarization at scale (90s+ tails on peak).
- High per-token cost from current setup; want better unit economics for embedding+rerank-heavy flows.
- Security: need audit logs and VPC options for PII-sensitive inference.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce 95th percentile generation latency to under 500ms for conversational flows.
- Cut embedding+rerank token cost by ~30% while keeping relevance stable.
- Deploy in a VPC/Private mode for regulated workloads within Q3.

Integration & fit notes (what we discussed):
- SDK changes: we support both REST and our official SDKs (Python/Node). The SDK now includes built-in streaming helpers and structured output validation to make tool/function-calling easier.
- Function calling: Redwood supports structured function call output (JSON schema validation) which maps directly to your extractor service. This avoids brittle regex parsing.
- Streaming: we can stream partial tokens to the client and provide chunk-level metrics for latency SLOs. Good fit for your real-time preview UX.
- Embeddings/reranking: we recommend embedding + ANN-based reranker with cold-cache caching for repeated queries. Quantized model variants provide 2-3x cost savings for dense embedding generation.

Attachments: redwood-solution-brief.pdf (high-level), redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (ballpark). Also linking a small integration sample.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (30-45m) with your infra team — propose Thu 3/5 10:00am PT or Fri 3/6 11:00am PT.
2) We'll share a short POC plan: sample dataset, success metrics (latency & cost targets), and rough timeline (2-4 weeks).
3) Security questionnaire and procurement intro when you signal readiness.

Can you confirm which time works for the technical deep-dive? I can send a calendar invite and include our infra lead (Dylan) and security lead (Neha) for the walkthrough.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

--

Thanks, Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) For streaming: we need token-level ordering guarantees and a way to abort mid-stream from the client (we already have a websocket-based preview). Is your streaming approach compatible with abort semantics?
2) For function calling: our extractor expects a strict JSON schema. Can you confirm Redwood will surface schema validation errors back to the client in a machine-readable way?
3) For pricing: procurement asked for a baseline pricing sheet and a sample committed throughput discount cadence. Can you attach the pricing PDF?

We can do Thu 3/5 10:00am PT. Add our infra lead (Ben Carter) if helpful.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Search & Relevance
Acme Corp
alex@acme-corp.com

Alex — thanks, great questions. Short answers and follow-ups below.

Streaming/abort semantics:
- Yes — our streaming API supports client-side aborts. The SDK exposes a cancel() handle for in-flight streams. When aborted we still emit partial metrics and can mark the request as aborted in logs for auditing.

Function calling / schema validation:
- We validate JSON against provided schemas server-side. When a validation error occurs we return a structured error payload (error.code, error.field, error.reason) so your extractor can handle failures programmatically.

Pricing / procurement:
- Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (baseline + committed throughput tiers). For deals of this size we typically offer a 20% discount at the 12-month reserved capacity tier; we can scope exact numbers after the POC.

Reminders for the tech deep-dive:
- We'll demo streaming latency with a 2-minute live run (sample data).
- Show embedding generation latency and ANN reranking throughput.
- Bring a short section on structured outputs and function-call failure modes.

Meeting invite: https://calendly.com/redwood/tech-deep-dive-acme (Thu 3/5 10:00am PT)

I attached a small integration sample (integration-sample.zip) with SDK snippets for streaming + function-calling. If you want Ben on the call, add him and I’ll include a short procurement/finance intro.

Best,
Marissa

--
